_meta.indication: IBRANCE is indicated in combination with letrozole for the treatment of postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer as initial endocrine-based therapy for their metastatic disease; approved under accelerated approval based on PFS.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 1/2, open-label, randomized study (Phase 2 part formed the basis of the NDA)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multicenter study of palbociclib plus letrozole versus letrozole alone; randomization stratified by disease site and disease-free interval.
pivotal_trials.population: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had not received previous systemic treatment for their advanced disease.
pivotal_trials.n: 165 patients randomized to Phase 2 (palbociclib + letrozole N=84; letrozole N=81).
pivotal_trials.result: Median investigator-assessed PFS 20.2 months (palbociclib + letrozole) vs 10.2 months (letrozole alone); HR=0.488 (95% CI 0.319-0.748).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) were neutropenia, leukopenia, fatigue, anemia, upper respiratory infection, nausea, stomatitis, alopecia, diarrhea, thrombocytopenia, decreased appetite, vomiting, asthenia, peripheral neuropathy, and epistaxis. Neutropenia all grades 75% (Grade 3 48%, Grade 4 6%) with IBRANCE + letrozole. Most frequent serious adverse reactions were pulmonary embolism (3 of 83; 4%) and diarrhea (2 of 83; 2%).
target_moa: Palbociclib is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4 and 6; Cyclin D1 and CDK4/6 are downstream of signaling pathways that lead to cellular proliferation, and palbociclib blocks progression from G1 into S phase of the cell cycle.

advisory_committee.vote: The NDA was not presented for discussion at an Advisory Committee meeting because outside expertise was not necessary.
